1509c69108ad.english: Total NMDA-receptor reduction, a GluN2A-weighted component, a general loss of drive, and a bath-state (magnesium, potassium) effect.

19df3deb1317.english: A residual fall beyond a control matched to the same measured current reduction, together with a loss of coupling, keeps the connexin question open.

1b2acaee70e8.english: An explicit statement of the recording conditions, or recordings under blockade with identity by morphology and matched access resistance.

26884cb86182.english: The burst may also need AMPA-receptor drive. This is exploratory; the premise is not established.

2d0bcfbcaf77.english: A curve shifted to the left of the full-antagonist curve, with a measured sensitive fraction, makes the GluN2B-directed comparison the better question.

2d13a2f2e87f.english: Sag and rebound are larger in the knockout; no Ih-blocker arm and no voltage-clamp current exist in the records read. In normal cortex an Ih blocker reduces sag.

2f60e5178da3.english: Is the NMDA-receptor dependence total receptor gain or GluN2B-weighted?

345a9097699c.english: The passive and leak reading (MH1), a T-type contribution to rebound, off-target sodium-current block of the tool, another HCN isoform or compartment.

368203a08734.english: Smaller cells with a fixed seal leak, a larger Ih, selection by input-resistance criteria, maturation delay, and a cell-type mix.

3863daef052a.english: A matched-condition excess sag blocked by both chemotypes with a larger voltage-clamp Ih density would move HCN from 'contributes' to 'differs'.

4a2b9abb49f6.english: Does an Ih (HCN) contribution remain after matching potential and deflection?

4ea9ffac88e8.english: The numbers do not fit a pure loss of resting K+ conductance at constant capacitance; smaller cells plus a conductance change is one reading. Capacitance is not an established difference. No drug is proposed.

4effcdba3c5d.english: In the neuron-specific knockout slice an NMDA-receptor antagonist abolishes the spontaneous bursts. No AMPA/kainate antagonist has been applied; a shift of the knockout excitatory-current amplitude fits an AMPA-type quantum only by inference.

4f83df16e380.english: Can the gap-junction tool's burst fall be read as a gap-junction result?

62aca19854ba.english: Do passive cell size and a resting K+ conductance explain the larger sag and input resistance?

681925371373.english: An HCN contribution may remain after matching conditions. This is a tool arm only: two blocker chemotypes, engagement first. No candidate drug and no in-vivo claim.

6cc825d7ca20.old_english: Repeat the slice burst assay with the magnesium concentration reported, a d-APV arm and a GluN2B NAM arm, each at matched measured NMDAR-current reduction (two unrelated NAMs), vehicle time-matched, animal as the unit; memantine only afterwards, with the magnesium concentration and holding voltage stated, beside the tool compound, and the untreated same-genotype comparator.
6cc825d7ca20.added_english: [IT40] B6 Report bath magnesium, K+, temperature and blockers actually present as measured values; use a within-slice paired design; add an AMPA/kainate block arm verified by the fast EPSC (abolition alone is not informative, because loss of magnesium relief would abolish an NMDAR-regenerative burst too); add a matched-effect control read on at least two metrics with a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; add a GABA-A arm because the sIPSC amplitude is halved; state the order of application and washout as part of the design.

6ee3608f2a55.english: The Methods drug list contains no synaptic blocker, so the intrinsic recordings were probably made with synapses intact, while most knockout slices burst.

7a468e0dc06b.english: A genuine cell-autonomous difference (MH1 or MH2), maturation delay, a cell-type mix.

7feead3ba9ed.old_english: In knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices: sag, resting potential, input resistance, rebound and burst incidence before and after two Ih blockers of different chemotypes (the second so that an off-target action is not read as Ih), with a current-clamp step that matches the resting potential and the peak potential, with a smaller cell or immature membrane listed as its own candidate beside branch D, and a voltage-clamp read of the blocker-sensitive current in a subset of cells; animals, not cells, are the replicates. Branch D adds the potassium-current arm: the potassium currents sensitive to a Kv7 blocker and to a Kir-channel blocker in voltage clamp, and input resistance read with synaptic transmission blocked. [IT36] A first-generation Ih blocker at 50 uM is about 40 times its sodium-current IC50 in DRG neurons (age not stated); read a second chemotype and the blocker-sensitive current in voltage clamp; nickel/Z944 and Kv7 arms separate.
7feead3ba9ed.added_english: [IT40] A4 Report access resistance, bridge balance and capacitance by genotype; add a Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive difference current with its zero-crossing against E_K (about -97 to -98 mV from the declared solutions; the recorded potentials need a junction correction of about -13 mV that 34634460 did not measure, which puts the estimated sag peaks about 16-21 mV below E_K, so the prediction applies to the voltage-clamp difference current, not to the sag peak).

80fa15bc6765.english: Reduced release or altered excitability; direct NMDA-receptor channel block (neither shown nor excluded); neuronal electrical coupling; pannexin-1; run-down or a recording artefact.

81fba8b46d33.english: If the excess vanishes at matched conditions, or the blocker-sensitive current per pF is the same, there is no HCN difference. A blocker response shows contribution, not a defect.

87177877f044.english: If sag remains at matched potential and deflection, or capacitance is unchanged while input resistance is higher, the passive reading fails.

896cd43acd21.english: Coincident curves make total NMDA-receptor reduction (with the bath magnesium and voltage) the question; a plateau below abolition moves it to GluN2A-containing receptors. None of this can come from other preparations.

8c0bcfdd6eff.english: A GluN2B-selective negative modulator may remove the bursts at a smaller measured fraction of the isolated NMDA-receptor current than the full antagonist needs. Exploratory.

929dc08517c1.english: Capacitance and time constant measured in the same cells, or a Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive difference current in Wwox neurons, would decide whether any pharmacological arm is needed.

9671de4502ca.english: The burst needs NMDA-receptor activity; about 20 percent of the delayed evoked response remains against the wild-type floor under the antagonist, which is not evidence of incomplete block.

9c53196383de.old_english: WWOX-system, one preparation read in full and re-extracted (PMID 34634460, Table 1 and Figure 6): resting potential -79.25, -75.51, -73.62 mV and sag at a fixed -200 pA step 1.18, 2.04, 2.57 mV grade with gene dose, input resistance saturates at one allele, rebound is marked larger only in the knockout (the printed p cannot be reproduced from the Table 1 means and dispersion under stated assumptions), and bursts occur in 36 of 42 knockout, 4 of 23 heterozygote and 0 of 11 wild-type slices; the authors name control of the resting membrane potential as a factor underlying the hyperexcitability (the frequency-current slope does not differ once the curves are shifted to one step below rheobase; supplement not read) and cite discordant Ih-blocker precedents, including worsening of 4-AP events. Compound side: Ih-acting tools exist in the catalogue (a clinically used HCN blocker and several research blockers, identities resolved), found by the need search without naming any; their cellular potency in a cortical pyramidal neuron and their selectivity among HCN isoforms were not assessed here. No Ih-blocker experiment in a Wwox-deficient preparation is recorded in the entries read. [IT39] Ivabradine blocks sag and hyperpolarises cortical L5 and L6 neurons in normal rat slices, and injection into somatosensory cortex cut absence-seizure time by 96 percent against 40 percent in thalamic VB (abstract); the GAERS authors read Ih as not an adaptive response to spike-wave discharges (input resistance fell, resting potential and sag unchanged), which sits beside the discordant precedents.

a5fde891ed17.english: Part of the contrast may reflect network state or cell selection rather than a cell-autonomous difference. This is a design control; no drug is proposed.

aedc0c4f5ce9.english: A gap-junction-blocking tool lowered the burst rate in the knockout slice and did not recover. In culture the same tool lowers AMPA and NMDA currents, broadens spikes and lowers input resistance.

af1905e427d4.english: Does the burst depend on AMPA-receptor drive?

b719c7c10191.english: A verified AMPA/kainate block that abolishes the bursts at less total charge removed than the NMDA-receptor antagonist needs would put AMPA receptors first in the next question.

c49c9b6c64b0.english: Were the intrinsic recordings made under conditions that bias the genotype contrast?

d93e57bc7da0.old_english: Whether a partial, clinically achievable block suffices, and whether the carded effect is a subunit effect or a pore-block effect. A pore blocker's potency depends on voltage and on magnesium, so the unreported bath is itself the obstacle. [IT36] A GluN2B NAM effect would show participation of GluN2B-containing receptors in sustaining bursts, not that the lesion lies in GluN2B; it needs a target-specific control (matched-current d-APV).
d93e57bc7da0.added_english: [IT40] B5 Radiprodil is GluN2B-selective in oocytes (the selectivity sentence rests on an unread supplementary figure) with 45 percent maximum inhibition of GluN2A/GluN2B triheteromers and very slow washout; its use or activity dependence was not tested; its slice precedent is CA1 at P17-P22 with bath magnesium stated as 1.5 mM in the Methods and 0.2 mM in the legends. TCN-201 acts on recombinant GluN2A only, potency set by glycine, maximum inhibition 73-81 percent, so a TCN-201 arm needs a measured slice co-agonist level.

dab8f9799b5d.english: If a matched non-gap-junction control gives the same fall, the gap-junction attribution is not supported; a pannexin-1 blocker with shown engagement that lowers bursts would support pannexin-1.

e0839859cc57.english: The fall may come from effects on synaptic currents and excitability rather than from coupling. No datum in the sources read supports the gap-junction half. Exploratory.

e6aa39a1f3a3.english: Input resistance rises 39 percent in mutants while the time constant is nearly unchanged; resting potential and sag grade with gene dose. Recordings use one fixed current step.

e814ea2de1be.english: If the contrast is unchanged under blockade with matched access resistance, it is intrinsic to the recorded membrane; if it shrinks, the original contrast was partly synaptic state or selection.

eaaec5adb8f1.english: Bursts that persist under a verified, pre-specified AMPA/kainate block weaken this reading. Abolition alone does not separate AMPA drive from NMDA-receptor-regenerative drive, because losing the depolarisation also removes magnesium relief.

ed04c567319d.english: NMDA-receptor-regenerative drive (GluN2B- or GluN2A-weighted), a general loss of excitatory drive, and a recording-state artefact. Kainate receptors are not separated from AMPA receptors by the usual tools.

f5b6c67dfba6.old_english: Branch A, compensatory Ih: blocking it worsens or leaves bursts; weakened if bursts fall. Branch B, pro-excitatory Ih through the depolarised resting potential: blocking it lowers bursts at matched membrane potential; weakened if bursts do not fall. Branch C, bystander: no effect on bursts although sag falls; weakened by any burst change. The sag itself must first be shown to be Ih (sensitive to the blocker), and a blocker that shifts the resting potential acts on the premises of A and B at once. Branch D, added from an unguided expansion (IT35): the higher input resistance of the knockout and the heterozygote is the opposite of what a larger Ih alone would give (in a rat cortical dysplasia model reduced Ih came with a higher input resistance, reversed by an Ih blocker, PMID 21795624; there the resting potential is hyperpolarised, so it is not a mirror image), so a second or alternative change, such as loss of a resting potassium conductance (Kir, K2P or Kv7 channels), is a rival explanation; weakened if blocker-sensitive potassium currents do not differ.
f5b6c67dfba6.added_english: [IT40] A3 Whether the excess sag and rebound persist at matched potential and matched deflection, whether capacitance differs, and whether the recordings were under synaptic blockade; only then whether a blocker-sensitive current differs. A blocker response shows that the current contributes, not that it is defective in Wwox cells.
